current_answer_short: Capital visibly reaches borrowers, infrastructure assets, energy systems, fleet/collateral pools, backlog execution, acquisition finance, and sponsor-backed platforms.
open_question: Which dollars are productive capacity versus acquisition, refinancing, liquidity, or control transfer?
working_hypothesis: The cycle is mixed: some dollars build capacity, some refinance or consolidate ownership, and some provide balance-sheet flexibility.
proof_mechanism: Classify each source row by destination type and use-of-proceeds class; separate audit rows, same-period exposure, and promoted totals.
next_documents: Sources-and-uses tables; credit agreements; merger proxies; rating reports; capex schedules; project budgets; borrower operating KPIs.
upgrade_rule: Upgrade when a named source document ties amount, period, vehicle, borrower, and use category together.
falsification_or_weaken_rule: Weaken if exposure rows cannot be tied to a borrower or the use is only broad liquidity with no operating destination.

meta_question: Who is the source of capital?
current_answer_short: Source wrappers are visible for BDCs, insurers, retirement-linked platforms, public debt investors, ABL/AR lenders, private-credit funds, and bank facilities.
open_question: Can ultimate investor money be tied to a named borrower in the same period?
working_hypothesis: Ultimate source differs by wrapper: BDC equity/debt, insurer liabilities, private fund LPs, securitization lenders, 144A buyers, or bank balance sheets.
proof_mechanism: Decompose each holder vehicle into liabilities, equity/NAV, leverage, investor base, facilities, and adviser/funding relationships.
next_documents: Vehicle annual reports; statutory Schedule D/BA; fund prospectuses; leverage tables; funding notes; credit-facility notes; adviser disclosures.
upgrade_rule: Upgrade when a vehicle's funding stack is visible in the same reporting period as the borrower exposure.
falsification_or_weaken_rule: Weaken if the vehicle is only named as holder and no funding-stack source is available.

current_answer_short: The Ares borrower expansion classifies visible holder/source vehicles across BDCs, non-traded/private-credit funds, registered funds, private funds, direct-lending programs, and transaction sources.
open_question: Which liabilities or investor bases fund each vehicle's assets?
working_hypothesis: Vehicle identity is mostly solved for visible holder rows; capital-stack decomposition is the next layer.
proof_mechanism: Create one capital-stack row per recurring holder with asset base, liabilities, NAV/equity, leverage, investor base, adviser, and source visibility.
next_documents: Vehicle annual reports; 10-Q/10-K schedules; prospectuses; adviser agreements; subscription materials where public; facility notes.
upgrade_rule: Upgrade when holder identity, manager, vehicle type, source visibility, and funding stack are all documented.
falsification_or_weaken_rule: Weaken if vehicle names are ambiguous, stale, renamed, or not matched to the borrower schedule period.

meta_question: What does the capital fund in the real economy?
current_answer_short: Named destinations include roadway safety, aerospace MRO, wealth management, insurance brokerage, refrigeration/foodservice equipment, precision manufacturing, building maintenance, automotive services, fleet, LNG/midstream, and grid assets.
open_question: Which flows are organic growth, capacity buildout, acquisition, refinancing, rescue, dividend, or working capital?
working_hypothesis: Power/grid, LNG, fleet, and backlog lanes lean toward physical output; several private-credit borrower lanes lean toward acquisition finance and consolidation.
proof_mechanism: Use use-of-proceeds classifications, then upgrade with legal documents or operating evidence that names the actual use.
next_documents: Credit agreements; merger proxies; funds-flow language; sponsor releases; capex schedules; project budgets; acquisition timelines; borrower KPIs.
upgrade_rule: Upgrade when the use category is tied to a named amount and borrower event or operating program.
falsification_or_weaken_rule: Weaken if only generic growth language exists or transaction value is used as a proxy for debt/use.

meta_question: Does the capital convert into output?
current_answer_short: URI, Sterling, power/grid, and energy lanes have partial output evidence through fleet productivity, OEC, backlog, cash conversion, dockets, tariffs, ESAs, cargo/export, and projects.
open_question: Does capital create incremental output and durable cash flow, or just a larger balance sheet?
working_hypothesis: Operating bottleneck companies matter where capital meets scarce assets, regulated recovery, fleet density, project control, or recurring service demand.
proof_mechanism: Score each lane on repeated-period output metrics and cash conversion after the financing or investment period.
next_documents: Revenue; EBITDA; cash conversion; utilization; OEC; MW in service; cargo volumes; rate-base additions; backlog burn; capex-to-output; project milestones.
upgrade_rule: Upgrade when output metric movement can be tied to the funded period and persists beyond one quarter.
falsification_or_weaken_rule: Weaken if capex/backlog grows without utilization, revenue, cash conversion, or project in-service proof.

meta_question: Is private credit replacing banks or sitting beside them?
current_answer_short: Auctane/Stamps.com confirms selected bank takeout; Medallia is strong but incomplete; Atwell remains plausible but unresolved; broad bank disappearance is not proven.
open_question: Do banks remain through revolvers, agency, treasury, hedging, collateral facilities, or ancillary roles?
working_hypothesis: Private credit often replaces or supplements bank term debt while banks remain elsewhere in the capital stack.
proof_mechanism: Build pre/post lender maps and search for repayment, termination, amendment, agent, revolver, hedging, and collateral-facility evidence.
next_documents: Credit-agreement terminations; payoff notices; UCC amendments; new credit agreements; lender lists; rating reports; agent names; bank denominator data.
upgrade_rule: Upgrade when old bank facility status and new private-credit facility role are both visible.
falsification_or_weaken_rule: Weaken if banks remain as agent/revolver/collateral lenders or if only secondary source bank-competition language exists.

meta_question: Is the evidence borrower-specific or only platform-scale?
current_answer_short: Platform disclosures prove scale; BDC schedules and borrower crosswalks prove named exposure.
open_question: Can platform pools be tied to named borrower assets without unsupported allocation claims?
working_hypothesis: The defensible chain is platform scale -> vehicle stack -> holder row -> borrower -> facility/use -> output.
proof_mechanism: Keep platform metrics and borrower exposure in separate tables, then join only through same-period vehicle, borrower, instrument, and source evidence.
next_documents: Same-period vehicle reports; borrower schedules; facility documents; transaction documents; source-of-capital notes.
upgrade_rule: Upgrade when platform, vehicle, borrower, instrument, period, and amount all line up.
falsification_or_weaken_rule: Weaken if AUM/deployment is used as borrower allocation proof or if holder rows are stale relative to the transaction.

current_answer_short: The Ares borrower lane separates row-level audit sums, master-rollup promoted totals, and a 9-row same-period borrower control.
open_question: Which number should be used in external writing?
working_hypothesis: Audit rows are for coverage, same-period controls are for conservative snapshots, and master rollups are for promoted latest-visible totals.
proof_mechanism: Enforce row type, period, duplicate, same-period, and allowed-use controls in generated tables.
next_documents: Generated audit tables; master rollups; same-period summaries; duplicate rules; claim-use notes.
upgrade_rule: Upgrade when every promoted number has a documented permitted-use field and period rule.
falsification_or_weaken_rule: Weaken if mixed-period, comparative, transaction-only, locator, or derived rows are summed as current exposure.

meta_question: What are the limits of every claim?
current_answer_short: The promoted-claims system tracks safe claims and overclaims for facility size, transaction value, AUM, commitments, and durability.
open_question: Which claims are publication-ready versus internal leads?
working_hypothesis: Level 4 claims can be used with boundaries; Level 5 claims can use stronger mechanism language; Level 2-3 claims remain leads.
proof_mechanism: Run every claim through primary-source, amount, period, actor, mechanism, contrary-role, and boundary checks.
next_documents: Claim scorecard; promoted-claims register; contrary-source checks; source documents; what-it-says fields.
upgrade_rule: Upgrade when a claim has a source-backed mechanism plus clear overclaim boundaries.
falsification_or_weaken_rule: Weaken if any claim depends on inference without source, period, amount, actor, or contrary-role check.

meta_question: Can this scale across the 519-company universe?
current_answer_short: The operating pieces exist: evidence ledger, source queue, claim scorecard, triage table, lane queues, taxonomy, holder expansion, same-period controls, source bridge, bank-role pass, and use-of-proceeds pass.
open_question: Can every company be classified by role, wrapper, proof metric, and missing evidence?
working_hypothesis: The scalable unit is company -> role -> wrapper -> source document -> metric -> claim strength -> missing proof.
proof_mechanism: Run a repeatable extraction template across all companies and assign lane, role, wrapper, source availability, proof level, denominator need, next document, and safe claim.
next_documents: Company reports; filings; lane queues; source availability scoring; denominator maps; extraction scripts.
upgrade_rule: Upgrade when each company has a complete role/wrapper/proof/missing-evidence row.
falsification_or_weaken_rule: Weaken if the case-study set remains disconnected from the full 519-company universe.
